title: Nicotine Addiction and the Risk to the Older Adolescent Despite Awareness
summary: Nicotine addiction in adolescents develops faster than they expect after the first try. Signs of addiction include: an overwhelming urge to smoke, anxiety without it, and failed attempts to quit. If you notice these signs in your son, seek help from a doctor or specialist immediately; most who quit need more than one attempt, and professional support greatly increases the chance of success, according to HealthyChildren.org, affiliated with the American Academy of Pediatrics. A sixteen- or seventeen-year-old adolescent knows the harms of smoking well, but his brain is not yet fully developed (development continues until the mid-twenties), so the desire to fit in with friends remains stronger than his awareness of danger in the moment of actual pressure, according to the U.S. National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH). Do not consider his proximity to adulthood a guarantee of immunity from pressure; continue open dialogue rather than just scolding.
try_this: This week: Start a calm conversation with your son about his friends and who might be smoking around him, without direct accusation. Ask him frankly if he has tried or is thinking of trying it, and listen without immediate scolding.
reflection_prompts: Do you believe that your son’s knowledge of the harms is enough to protect him on its own?
If you notice an early sign of addiction in your son, do you know who to turn to immediately?
